generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

[[ if test="member(1, ta_index)" ]]

The term "Measure of Dispersion" refers to the study of the scatteredness or spread of observations within a data set. It is used to quantify how data points in a dataset are dispersed or spread out from the central tendency, typically represented by measures such as the mean or median.

[[/ if ]] [[ if test="member(2, ta_index)" ]]

The study of the scatteredness of observations is known as "Measure of Spread." This is a concept in statistics that describes how data points in a dataset are spread out or dispersed. The most common measures of spread include the range, variance, standard deviation, and interquartile range. These measures help to quantify the extent to which data points deviate from the central tendency (such as the mean or median) and provide insights into the variability or dispersion of the data.

[[/ if ]]
